contract-break.message: sender web sends `giftNote: string`; receiver orders-api declares no such field; the receiver does not declare it, and its validation pipe forbids what it does not whitelist, so a request sending it is refused with 400

sse-event-unhandled.message: GET /orders/events sends frames as the event "order-ready", which LiveService.onReady never listens for: it listens for "message", and onmessage hears only frames named no event
sse-event-unhandled.evidence: every frame the route writes was read with its name, and every listener of the stream with the name it listens for
sse-event-unhandled.fix: listen with addEventListener("order-ready", …), or send the frames with no event name

bot-button-unhandled.message: ShopBot.showOrder builds a button sending "order:track", which no handler of callback data matches; the handlers match "order:confirm", "order:tracking", /^order:cancel:(\w+)$/, /^order:details:/
bot-button-unhandled.evidence: every handler of callback data in the project was read, and none takes every callback

bot-button-data-too-long.message: ShopBot.showOrder builds a button whose callback data "order:details:with-the-full-delivery-address-and-the-courier-notes" is 66 bytes, over the 64 the bot platform takes: the message carrying it is refused
bot-button-data-too-long.evidence: the bot platform's API takes callback_data of 1-64 bytes; the data is written out
bot-button-data-too-long.fix: send a short key (an id, a code) and look the rest up when it comes back

config-name-mismatch.message: PAYMENT_API_KEY is read with no default by OrdersService.list and set nowhere, while PAYMENTS_API_KEY is set in .env.example and read nowhere
config-name-mismatch.evidence: one name is read and set nowhere, the other set and read nowhere, a letter or two apart
config-name-mismatch.fix: one name spelled two ways: read PAYMENTS_API_KEY, or set PAYMENT_API_KEY

status-never-answered.message: OrderPanelComponent.cancel branches on 410 from POST /orders/:param/cancel, which never answers 410: it answers 404, 409
status-never-answered.evidence: every failure of the route was read with its status and nothing behind it left unread; statuses a proxy or the framework may answer (400, 401, 403, 408, 413, 429, 5xx) are not judged
status-never-answered.fix: branch on what the route answers (404, 409), or make it answer 410

cors-credentials.message: OrdersApiService.list (GET /orders) sends credentials to orders-api, whose CORS answers any origin with *: the browser blocks the answer
cors-credentials.evidence: the service enables CORS at src/main.ts:9, for a browser on another origin, and the setting was read
cors-credentials.fix: allow the front end's origin by name (origin: [...], or true to echo it) with credentials: true

cors-header-not-allowed.message: OrdersApiService.cancel (POST /orders/:param/cancel) sets x-request-id, which orders-api's CORS does not allow (it allows authorization, content-type): the browser's preflight fails
cors-header-not-allowed.evidence: the service enables CORS at src/main.ts:9, for a browser on another origin, and the setting was read
cors-header-not-allowed.fix: add x-request-id to allowedHeaders, or leave allowedHeaders out to allow what the browser asks for

cors-method-not-allowed.message: OrdersApiService.remove (DELETE /orders/:param) uses DELETE, which orders-api's CORS does not allow (it allows GET, PATCH, POST): the browser's preflight fails
cors-method-not-allowed.evidence: the service enables CORS at src/main.ts:9, for a browser on another origin, and the setting was read

config-not-set.message: REDIS_URL is read with no default by OrdersService.create, and none of orders-api's deployment files sets it (.env.example, docker-compose.yml)
config-not-set.evidence: every deployment file of the service was read for the names it sets; a value given outside the files (a secret store, a console, the shell) is what would make this wrong
config-not-set.fix: set REDIS_URL where orders-api is deployed, or give the read a default

bot-handler-untriggered.message: ShopBot.track handles callback data "order:tracking", which no button the project builds sends; the buttons send "order:cancel:${…}", "order:confirm", "order:details:with-the-full-delivery-address-and-the-courier-notes", "order:track"
bot-handler-untriggered.evidence: every button the project builds was read with its callback data; a button built outside the project is what would make this wrong

config-never-read.message: LEGACY_EXPORT_DIR is set in .env.example and no code of orders-api reads it
config-never-read.evidence: every read of a setting in the service names its key; a library reading it by itself is what would make this wrong

config-not-set.why: the configuration module in src/app.module.ts validates the settings with a schema, which may give it a default

status-never-answered.why: POST /orders/:param/refund throws HttpException, whose status is not read
